rich_summary: Lomasa recounts how the celestial twin physicians, the Aswins, encounter Sukanya just after bathing and marvel at her beauty. Learning she is the devoted wife of the aged sage Chyavana, they tempt her to abandon him, promising pleasure and youth. Sukanya refuses, affirming her fidelity, but relays their proposal to Chyavana: the twins will restore his youth if she later chooses among the three of them. Chyavana agrees. After all three emerge from a sacred pool in identical youthful forms, Sukanya correctly recognizes and chooses her husband, proving her loyalty. Grateful, Chyavana promises the Aswins a share of the sacred Soma. When King Saryati later performs a sacrifice, Chyavana attempts to grant them this privilege, provoking Indra’s objection and setting up a confrontation over whether the Aswins deserve divine status.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces the encounter between Sukanya and the celestial Aswins, establishing the central temptation and moral test.
The Aswins admire Sukanya’s beauty and question why she serves an aged husband, framing the emotional and ethical tension.
Sukanya declares her unwavering devotion to Chyavana, the key moral statement of the episode.
The miraculous transformation scene where Chyavana and the Aswins emerge identical and youthful, creating the test of recognition.
Chyavana promises to grant the Aswins a share of Soma, which becomes the theological and political conflict with Indra.

top_scenes.scene_text: Sukanya standing by the forest pool just after bathing while the radiant twin Aswins approach her through the trees, astonished by her beauty.
Three identical youthful figures—Chyavana and the twin Aswins—emerge shining from a sacred pool as Sukanya studies them to recognize her true husband.
At the sacrificial altar, Chyavana calmly prepares Soma for the Aswins while Indra, thunderbolt raised in anger, threatens him before the gathered gods.
